description:
FILED s532d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while fixing #3961.  PRE-EXISTING (deterministic; base 06a4b8ba the same on a cold cache).

Both lowering paths call `_merge_module_prototypes($menv, undef, $module)` for a `require NAME` (Pl/Parser2.pm's use-statement pre-pass, the `require` arm; Pl/Parser.pm's v1 twin), and an undef import list takes the "import every codegen-relevant prototype" arm: the required module's (and its own imports') prototypes land in the requirer's flat table, sited at the require statement (#2871).  perl: `require` runs at run time and calls no import, so it changes NOTHING about how the requiring file was parsed; an unqualified call reaches the module's sub only through an import or a sub of the requirer's own package.
REPRODUCER: perl's CPAN/FirstTime.pm (lib 5.40.3) -- `require CPAN::Nox;` at line 866 (CPAN::Nox's walk carries ExtUtils::MakeMaker's prompt($;$)); FirstTime's own `sub prompt ($;$)` is at line 2194, BELOW every call, so perl compiles all 25 prompt() calls as LIST calls ("called too early to check prototype").  After s532d (#3961 fixed the cold/warm flip and `use M ()`), `pl2cl --module` emits 25 detector rows ("CPAN::FirstTime" "prompt" N "proto:$;$") for the calls at lines 887 .. 2125 -- every one below line 866.  A ($;$) slot imposes scalar context on the argument: silent wrong for an array / list-returning argument.
A minimal fixture: lib/RqA.pm = `package RqA; use Exporter 'import'; our @EXPORT = qw(p); sub p ($;$) { "A" } 1;`, lib/RqB.pm = `package RqB; sub go { require RqA; my @a = (5, 6); return p(@a) } sub p { "B:$_[0]" } 1;` -- perl RqB::go() is "B:5"; PCL reads p(@a) with ($;$) if the flat merge applies (probe it).
FIX SHAPE (not designed -- MEASURE first): the `require NAME` arm keeps the per-PACKAGE registration (a qualified call `RqA::p(...)` after a require is parsed with the prototype in perl only if RqA was loaded at COMPILE time -- even that is debatable) and drops the flat merge; corpus-diff + the four populations decide.  Watch a `require` of a package-less file of subs in the requirer's package (the `require "x.pl"` path is _extract_file_prototypes, separate; a `require NAME` whose file has no package statement defines subs in the CURRENT package and does need the flat facts).
subject: A `require Module` merges the module's codegen prototypes into the requiring file's FLAT table from the require's line on -- perl's require never imports and never changes the requirer's parse: CPAN::FirstTime's `require CPAN::Nox` (line 866) makes its own prompt() calls below it parse with ExtUtils::MakeMaker's ($;$)
